cases.question: What recalls are there for a 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
A 2017 Honda Civic has 6 NHTSA recalls on file. None are marked "park it" or "park outside." Some only cover certain body styles (sedan, coupe or hatchback), so tell me which one you have, or give me the VIN, and I'll check which ones apply.

For all 2017 Civic models listed by NHTSA:
- 18V663000 (steering): The steering magnet can come loose, causing unintended steering input and higher crash risk. Dealers replace the steering gearbox free of charge.
- 23V858000 (fuel pump): The fuel pump may fail and stall the engine. Dealers replace the fuel pump module free of charge.
- 26V332000 (passenger seat weight sensor): The sensor can short and cause air bags to deploy unintentionally in a crash. Dealers replace it free of charge. Owner letters went out July 7, 2026.

Body-style-specific recalls:
- 17V706000 (sedan and coupe): The right halfshaft may break, which can allow a roll-away if the parking brake isn't set. Dealers inspect and replace it free of charge.
- 18V266000 (hatchback): The front seatback pads lack slits for the side air bags, which can interfere with deployment. Dealers replace the pads free of charge.
- 18V817000 (hatchback): The owner's guide may be missing required child-seat anchor information. Dealers replace the kit free of charge.

For an official status check on your car, go to nhtsa.gov/recalls and enter the VIN. Honda customer service: 1-888-234-2138.

cases.question: Is there a power steering recall on the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Yes, NHTSA lists one electric power steering recall for the 2017 Honda Civic: campaign 18V663000.

What it covers: the magnet that reads the steering torque sensor may not be secured and can come loose. During a full-lock turn, steering assist may be applied in the opposite direction, which reduces maneuverability and raises the risk of a crash.

The fix: Honda dealers will replace the steering gearbox assembly at no charge. Owners can call Honda at 1-888-234-2138.

This recall is not marked "park it" or "park outside."

Your car's body style isn't settled yet, and I can't confirm from here that this recall covers your specific car. If you send me your 17-character VIN, I'll decode it and check. You can also check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls for official status.

answer.text:

cases.question: Is there a recall for the halfshaft or driveshaft on a 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Yes, there is one halfshaft recall for the 2017 Honda Civic: campaign 17V706000. It covers 2017 Civic Sedan and Coupe vehicles. The right halfshaft may have been improperly heat treated, which can cause it to break. A broken halfshaft can stop the car from moving and allow a roll-away if the parking brake isn't engaged. Honda will inspect the halfshaft's serial number, replace it if needed, and align the front wheels, free of charge. Owners can call Honda at 1-888-234-2138 (Honda's number for this recall is K0E).

This recall does not cover the 2017 Civic Hatchback. What body style is your car: sedan, coupe, or hatchback? If you send your 17-character VIN, I can confirm the body style. You can also check the VIN's recall status at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

cases.question: Which air bag recalls are listed for the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
NHTSA lists two air bag recalls for the 2017 Honda Civic:

1. 26V332000 (air bag sensor, front passenger seat). The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, so the air bags could deploy unintentionally in a crash. Dealers will replace the sensors free of charge. This recall covers the 2016-2022 Civic, which includes 2017 models. Owner letters were mailed July 7, 2026.

2. 18V266000 (air bags, seat pads). This applies only to the 2017 Civic Hatchback and Civic Type R. Replacement front seatback pads were made without slits for the side air bags, which could block them from deploying. Dealers will replace the pads free of charge.

Neither recall is marked "park it" or "park outside."

Recall status depends on the exact car, so please share your VIN or body style (sedan, coupe or hatchback). You can also check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

cases.question: What recalls does a 2006 Ford Ranger have?

answer.text:
Warning: Do not drive your 2006 Ford Ranger until it is repaired if it has recall 18V022000, 18V023000, 17V787000 or 17V788000. NHTSA marks these "park it" because the air bag inflators can explode or rupture in a crash. Call Ford at 1-866-436-7332 or see a dealer now.

NHTSA lists 12 recall campaigns for the 2006 Ford Ranger:

Air bag inflator recalls:
- 18V022000 (passenger side, Ford 18S02): do not drive until repaired. The inflator may explode.
- 18V023000 (driver side, Ford 18S02): do not drive until repaired. The inflator may explode.
- 17V787000 (driver side, Ford 17S42): do not drive until repaired. The inflator may rupture. This supersedes 16V036000.
- 17V788000 (passenger side, Ford 17S42): do not drive until repaired. The inflator may rupture. This supersedes 15V322000.
- 16V036000 (driver side, Ford 16S03): interim repair, replaced by 17V787000.
- 15V322000 (passenger side, Ford 15S22): inflator may rupture from moisture. Partly superseded by 17V788000.
- 21V076000 and 21V081000 (Ford 21S05): inflator may explode from long-term humidity and heat. Dealers will inspect and replace the module or inflator free.
- 23V125000 and 23V306000 (Ford 23S08): replacement passenger inflators may have been installed incorrectly. Dealers will reinstall them free. 23V306000 replaces 23V125000.

Other recalls:
- 11V352000 (Ford): tail, turn and brake lights may not work because of a faulty multi-function switch. Dealers replace the switch free.
- 05V520000: windshield wiper motor may lack grease and fail. Dealers inspect and grease it free. The NHTSA summary says "certain trucks," so check whether your truck is included.

NHTSA's list is by make, model and year, not by body style or VIN, so I have not confirmed each recall for your exact truck. For your VIN's official status, check nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you send me the VIN, I can decode it and check again.

cases.question: Does my 2019 Hyundai Tucson have any recalls?

answer.text:
Park it outside, away from buildings, until it is repaired: recall 20V543000 is marked "park outside" by NHTSA.

This is the one open recall listed for the 2019 Hyundai Tucson. The anti-lock brake control unit (HECU) can corrode and short electrically, which may cause an engine compartment fire.

What the recall covers: 2019-2021 Tucsons (and some 2016-2018 models) for the anti-lock brake control unit. Dealers will replace the HECU fuse, and for 2019-2021 models they will also update the Electronic Stability Control software. Repairs are free. To schedule it, call Hyundai customer service at 1-855-371-9460 (Hyundai recall number 195).

To confirm this recall applies to your exact car, check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you send me your VIN, I can decode it and check the details for you.

cases.question: Write me a Python function that sorts a list of numbers.

answer.text:
Here's a simple function that sorts a list of numbers and returns a new sorted list:

def sort_numbers(numbers):
    return sorted(numbers)

# Example
print(sort_numbers([5, 2, 9, 1, 7]))  # [1, 2, 5, 7, 9]

If you want to sort the list in place instead, use numbers.sort(). If you want to write the sorting algorithm yourself, I can do that too, for example bubble sort or merge sort.

cases.question: What are owners complaining about with the brakes on the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text: Owners have filed 39 brake-related complaints to NHTSA about the 2017 Honda Civic. Complaints are owners' own reports, not verified, and not recalls. The five newest describe: brake pedal locking or freezing with brake system warning lights (Sept 2026); electric parking brake engaging on its own after the car was off, on flat ground (Sept 2026); brakes squealing when stopping (Nov 2026); loud rear screeching while driving that stopped when the pedal was pressed (July 2025); and ABS and other warning lights on startup (Oct 2025). If the brakes lock, feel soft, or warning lights come on, have the car inspected right away. To check recall status for your car, enter its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, or send me your VIN and I can check recalls for it.

cases.question: Does recall 17V706000 apply to my 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Recall 17V706000 covers the 2017 Honda Civic Sedan and Coupe. It concerns the right halfshaft, which may have been improperly heat treated and could break. Honda's remedy is a free inspection of the halfshaft's serial number, replacement if needed, and a front wheel alignment. Honda's number for this recall is K0E.

Does your Civic have a sedan or coupe body? If you are not sure, the VIN will tell me. Send me the 17-character VIN and I'll check the body style. For the official status of your specific car, go to nhtsa.gov/recalls and enter your VIN. If you have a hatchback, this recall does not apply to it.

cases.question: Which recalls apply to my 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
NHTSA lists 6 recalls for the 2017 Honda Civic. None are marked "park it" or "park outside."

1. 18V663000: Electric power steering. A magnet may come loose, which can cause unintended steering input. Free fix: steering gearbox replacement.
2. 18V817000: Owner's manual/child seat anchorage info missing. Applies to the Civic Hatchback. Free fix: new owner's info kit.
3. 18V266000: Replacement front seatback pads lack slits for side air bags. Applies to the Civic Hatchback. Free fix: new seatback pads.
4. 17V706000: Right halfshaft may break, which can allow a roll-away if the parking brake isn't set. Applies to the Civic Sedan and Coupe. Free fix: inspection and replacement if needed.
5. 23V858000: Fuel pump may fail and stall the engine. Covers Civic Sedan, Coupe and Hatchback. Free fix: fuel pump module replacement.
6. 26V332000: Front passenger seat weight sensor may short, which can cause unintended air bag deployment in a crash. Covers the 2017 Civic Hatchback. Free fix: sensor replacement. Owner letters were mailed July 7, 2026.

Which ones apply to your car depends on its body style (sedan, coupe or hatchback). What is your car's body style? Or send me your 17-character VIN and I can check it. For official status on your specific car, check nhtsa.gov/recalls with the VIN.

cases.question: Does the air bag recall 18V266000 cover my 2017 Civic?

answer.text:
Recall 18V266000 covers only the 2017 Honda Civic Hatchback and Civic Type R. It does not cover the Civic Sedan or Coupe.

Which body style is your Civic? If you send your 17-character VIN, I can confirm it.

Also, NHTSA lists another air bag recall for 2016-2022 Civic models, 26V332000. It covers the front passenger seat weight sensor, which can crack and cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally in a crash. Dealers replace the sensor free of charge.

To check the official status of any recall on your specific car, go to nhtsa.gov/recalls and enter your VIN.
